I also want to make sure that we are focusing on the right things, and that is again making sure we have a good process,” he said. “But frankly, I want to make sure that more eligible voters in Michigan are doing what they need to do so that they can cast ballots.
findings.note: Quoted by Votebeat in its candidate Q&A, answering about non-citizen voting. He is quoted saying very few non-citizens cast ballots, and wants that number at zero while focusing on turnout of eligible voters.

findings.passage: Gilchrist said that voting is “reserved for citizens” and that anyone who votes despite not being a citizen needs “to be held accountable for that to the fullest extent of the law.” He also noted that “vanishingly few noncitizens … actually cast ballots.”
findings.note: Votebeat's sentence mixing its summary with short direct quotes from him on non-citizen voting. Only the quoted fragments are his own words.

findings.passage: We’re going to continue to make sure that our processes can be safe and secure,” he said. “I want to make sure that we are focused on the right thing. People having confidence in the voting process means that more people will participate in the voting process.
findings.note: Quoted by Votebeat on election security generally; no mention of ID.

findings.passage: On the question of non-citizens voting, an issue that gained attention this year after a citizens-only voting ballot petition failed to qualify, Gilchrist pointed to existing law. Addressing concerns about the state’s safeguards, he said, “It is already illegal. When it happens, people are held accountable for it. We have a system in place.”
